topic: How do interference models differ between co-frequency GEO and LEO systems when operating over the same service areas?
consensus_response: Co-frequency GEO and LEO systems experience distinct interference models due to their unique propagation characteristics and constellation geometries. The reduced spacing effects between LEO satellites lead to increased inter-satellite interference (ISI) due to the increased number of interfering signals, compromising system capacity. In contrast, GEO systems prioritize main beam alignment but sacrifice capacity due to fixed satellite positions. To mitigate inline interference, dynamic/flexible approaches like adaptive array processing and spatial multiplexing can be employed, requiring careful consideration of system/network implications.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges of co-frequency GEO and LEO systems operating over the same service areas, particularly in equatorial regions where earth stations' main beams align with both GEO and LEO satellites. The inline interference can be predetermined and avoided by using static and coordinated methods suggested by ITU R recommendations, but these methods may impact primary system performance and guarantee QoS for secondary LEO systems.
